title: The last progressive-seeding align calls run one deep query on one thread
body:
In progressive seeding, `seed_progressive` in `nail/src/pipeline/seed_stage.rs` runs `mmseqs align` once per iteration on a slice of the prefilter db. Each iteration doubles `n_take`, the number of candidates a still-active query takes. The active queries shrink to a handful, and the largest slice doubles every iteration.

On the 48-thread box at `bb3c392`, with the `stage-times` flags and inputs, the last four iterations ran with few cores busy:

| iteration | queries with pairs | largest query slice | wall, s | cpu |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 133 | 51,200 | 3.02 | 2729% |
| 9 | 41 | 102,400 | 3.86 | 1500% |
| 10 | 4 | 204,800 | 3.04 | 421% |
| 11 | 1 | 401,544 | 3.92 | 150% |

Together they took 13.8 s of the 34.4 s align total, in a 421.7 s run. Iterations 0 to 7 ran at 37 to 42 cores busy. At that rate the same work would take about 3 s, so the most this could recover is about 11 s, 2.6% of the run. That bound is arithmetic on the cpu column, not a measurement. The full table and the setup are in a note on nail-e52c52.

The cpu figures fit `mmseqs align` giving each query record of the prefilter db to one thread. Nobody has read the mmseqs source to confirm it.

## Open

- Whether `mmseqs align` accepts one query key in several prefilter records. If it does, nail could split a deep slice into pieces that run on separate threads.
- Whether a cap on `n_take` once few queries remain would change which seeds nail finds. Recall would have to be checked before making that trade.
